Thanks Amy — good to meet earlier today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we keep procurement moving: 

Summary (what I heard)
- CareSpan is evaluating Redwood for embedding inference in two product lines: clinical summarization (PHI) and analytics dashboards (non-PHI).
- Primary compliance concerns: SOC 2 scope for PHI, HIPAA Business Associate Agreement (BAA), GDPR data residency for EU customers, and a longer-term interest in FedRAMP for certain government pilots.
- You have an internal procurement + security review before legal can sign.

Open items we need to close for an initial procurement path
- Current SOC 2 status and scope (Type I/II, date, controls in-scope).
- Whether the clinical workload will require a BAA and any specific technical controls (encryption at rest, HSM/KMS).
- GDPR/DPA expectations and whether data residency in EU is required.
- Any vendor questionnaire or procurement portal items you want us to complete (I attached our standard consent and SOC scope stub).

Attachments: SOC2_Consent_and_Scope.pdf (stub), Redwood_Compliance_OnePager.pdf (linked in message)

Proposed next steps
1) Please share your vendor security questionnaire (or procurement portal link) — we can complete the technical sections quickly.
2) Schedule a 45-minute compliance deep-dive: Lauren (solutions/security engineer) + Neha (security PM) join to go through architecture and controls.
   - Proposed times: Wed 2026-09-23 09:00-09:45 PT or Fri 2026-09-25 11:00-11:45 PT. Tell us what works.
3) If SOC/HIPAA answers look good, we can provide a draft BAA and a commercial outline for the demo/proof-of-concept (timeline: 3–4 weeks).

If helpful I can also loop in our Trust & Safety lead to answer specific audit questions.

Thanks — I’ll keep this thread updated as we exchange docs.

—

Thanks Marcus — appreciated the clear summary. A few answers and notes from our side: 

SOC 2 / audits
- CareSpan currently has SOC 2 Type I (2025); Type II audit is in-flight with an expected report Q1 2027. We can share the Type I report and the SOC audit timeline.

HIPAA / PHI
- The clinical summarization workload will process limited PHI for covered provider customers. We require a BAA for any production PHI processing.
- Minimum technical asks: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest, and KMS integration for key separation.

GDPR / Data residency
- For EU customers we will require data residency in EU regions; at minimum, assurance that customer data can be stored/processed in eu-west-1.

FedRAMP
- FedRAMP is not a blocker for initial procurement but is a medium-term requirement for some pilots with federal partners. We would like to understand your roadmap and any FedRAMP-aligned controls.

Procurement artifacts
- Attached: CareSpan_Vendor_QS_v1.docx — our vendor questionnaire (partially filled; technical owners still need to confirm a few network and monitoring controls).
- Procurement portal: https://procure.carespan.com/portal/PO-4552 (we'll grant access once vendor approval begins).

Availability
- Wed 2026-09-23 09:00 PT works for a deep-dive. Please send a calendar invite. I’ll bring in our security engineer (cc: security@carespan.com) for the technical Q&A.

Thanks,
Amy

Initial clarifications from Redwood
- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II in 2025; we can provide the Type II report under NDA. I attached a short SOC2_Consent_and_Scope.pdf that outlines the controls and the evidence process.
- HIPAA / BAA: We have a standard BAA template and support KMS integration (customer-managed keys available for Dedicated/Private deployments).

- FedRAMP: We have a FedRAMP readiness program and a roadmap; timelines vary by program tier. We can provide the control mapping and a FedRAMP-readiness brief during the deep-dive.

Attachments: SOC2_Consent_and_Scope.pdf (attached)
